elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience ... by giving not less than ninety (90) days' prior notice, in writing"

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at not more than 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "any further charge payable by it by reason of such termination shall not exceed three (3) months of its share of Operation and Maintenance Costs"

elements.element: Vendor's convenience termination permitted only effective at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "any Party may terminate ... for convenience, including at any time during the Initial Period" — grants the counterparty a mid-term convenience exit

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term convenience termination requires 90 days' notice expressly
elements.evidence: No Vendor-specific end-of-term notice provision; only the generic "any Party ... ninety (90) days' prior notice"

elements.element: Customer may terminate on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "not less than ninety (90) days' prior notice"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on termination
elements.evidence: Only "The exclusion of credit for capital costs in Subparagraph 18.5 shall not apply"; no pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "any Party may terminate ... including at any time during the Initial Period"

offending_extra_words: any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience, including at any time during the Initial Period
The exclusion of credit for capital costs in Subparagraph 18.5 shall not apply to a termination under this Subparagraph 18.2A.
reasons: Fallback fails on a material term: the inserted right runs to "any Party", so the counterparty gains an unrestricted mid-term convenience exit rather than one exercisable only effective at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No express 90-day notice obligation is imposed on the counterparty for a permitted end-of-term convenience termination; the generic "any Party" formulation does not supply the asymmetric fallback bargain.

Not minimal: the symmetric "any Party ... at any time during the Initial Period" grant goes beyond what a Customer-side exit requires and hands the counterparty a benefit the playbook withholds; the added carve-out from the capital-cost credit exclusion is a separate economic concession not needed to complete the fallback.

Intent not preserved: the insertion cross-refers to "Subparagraph 18.5", which does not exist in this clause (the credit exclusion sits in the unnumbered paragraph referencing Subparagraph 18.1), creating a dangling mechanic; it also overrides 18.1 and 18.2's unanimity/one-year-notice architecture more broadly than needed.
Preferred is not met (90 days rather than 30, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no bar on counterparty convenience termination during the committed term).
